Anacomp Information Lifecycle

# From raw records to public release.

One information lifecycle pipeline for public agencies, sold end to end or one stage at a time.

Start a 30-day pilot
See the pipeline

- 01, Discover

- 02, Digitize

- 03, Redact

- 04, Remediate

- 05, Release

Analyze Insignal, across every stage, Ask Botcopy, answers from your documents

The problem

## Four pressures on agency records

Records programs are being asked to do more, faster, with files they can’t fully see, search, share or serve.

Visibility

### Unmapped file estates

Years of file shares and cloud folders, with no count of what is there or how much is duplicate.

Paper

### Paper that can’t be searched

Boxes and file rooms hold records that staff must pull by hand and cannot serve digitally.

Privacy

### Sensitive data in the open

PII sits inside unstructured documents, so nothing can be shared until someone reads every page.

Access

### Accessibility obligations

Section 508 and ADA Title II expect documents that work with assistive technology, not image-only PDFs.

The offering

## Five stages, one analytics layer

Six services. Each one is complete on its own, and each one’s output is the next one’s input.

Stage 1 · Discover

### Know what you hold before you move it

Congruity360 runs a shallow scan across file systems and cloud file repositories and returns the facts a records owner needs first.

What you receive

- File counts, sizes and types by location
- Duplicates identified for de-duplication
- A sized scope for any redaction or remediation that follows

Powered by

Congruity360

Stands alone when

You’re planning a cloud migration, a storage clean-up or an AI rollout and need an inventory first.

Leads to

Redact for sensitive files; Remediate for public-facing ones.

Stage 2 · Digitize

### Bring paper into the digital flow

Anacomp scanning services ingest paper documents and deliver indexed images that every later stage can work on.

What you receive

- Paper scanned and indexed to your scheme
- Digital files delivered to your repository or straight into the pipeline
- One digital starting point for redaction, accessibility and release

Powered by

Anacomp scanning services

Stands alone when

You have a paper backlog, a file-room closure or an electronic-records mandate to meet.

Leads to

Remediate, so scans become accessible data; Redact before anything is released.

Stage 3 · Redact

### Remove what must not be released

Anacomp redaction services remove PII and sensitive information from unstructured data, run as workflows on Hyperscience.

What you receive

- PII and sensitive content removed to your rules
- Redacted copies ready to release or share
- One process for scanned paper and born-digital files

Powered by

Hyperscience workflows, operated by Anacomp

Stands alone when

You face a records-request backlog, a litigation production or a data-sharing agreement.

Leads to

Release through the portal; Remediate so the redacted copy is also accessible.

Stage 4 · Remediate

### Turn any document into accessible data

ADA takes PDFs, Excel, PowerPoint, Word and image files, transcribes them, saves the content as data and republishes it in accessible form.

What you receive

- Accessible HTML for the web
- Accessibly tagged documents for download
- Content captured as data, ready for search and reuse

Powered by

Anacomp ADA

Stands alone when

You have an accessibility audit, complaint or mandate and a library of untagged documents.

Leads to

Release, to deliver accessible copies; Digitize, for paper still outside the library.

Ask the Document Powered by Botcopy

Put an accessible assistant beside the HTML that ADA produces, on your own site or portal. Residents ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn from the document whenever needed.

Stage 5 · Release

### Give the public a verified front door

The Anacomp portal lets members of the public, authenticated through ID.me, request documents that pass through the other stages before release.

What you receive

- Identity-verified document requests from the public
- Agency tools for requests, processing and client management
- A release step that can route through Digitize, Redact and Remediate first

Powered by

Anacomp portal with ID.me sign-in

Stands alone when

You need a request portal now and already have your own redaction or accessibility process.

Leads to

Every other stage: each request the portal takes in is work for them.

Across every stage · Analyze

### Ask your records program anything

Insignal builds a data warehouse from what the other stages produce and lets staff ask questions in plain English, then turn the answers into dashboards and alerts.

What you receive

- Estate dashboards from Discover scans: growth, duplicates, risk
- Operations dashboards: request volumes, turnaround, backlog
- Questions answered in plain English, in the browser or in Teams and Slack

Powered by

Insignal, self-hosted in your own cloud

Stands alone when

Leaders need to report on records work, or want answers from data that ADA has extracted.

Leads to

Discover, to feed it the estate; Release, to measure every request.

End to end

## A public records request, start to finish

From a verified request to an accessible, redacted release, in one chain of custody.

- 1

### Request

A member of the public verifies identity with ID.me and asks for documents in the portal.

- 2

### Locate

Agency staff pick up the request in the portal and find the records, on paper or in file stores.

- 3

### Digitize

Paper records are scanned and indexed.

- 4

### Redact

PII and sensitive content are removed in Hyperscience workflows.

- 5

### Remediate

ADA produces accessible HTML and a tagged document for download.

- 6

### Release

The agency approves and releases the documents to the requester in the portal.

Ask the Document, powered by Botcopy. Rather than scrolling through pages to find an answer, requesters just ask, and get a plain-language reply drawn from the document itself.

Records skip what they don’t need. Born-digital files bypass Digitize, and files with nothing sensitive bypass Redact.

Insignal, throughout. Every request is tracked, so staff can ask about volumes, turnaround and backlog in plain English.

How it is sold

## Two ways to buy

Option A

### The full pipeline

- One contract and one service level across every stage, with Insignal reporting on all of it

- Records move from stage to stage without leaving Anacomp custody

- The portal is the public’s front door and the agency’s work queue

Best for Agencies with steady request volume and a mix of paper and digital records.

Option B

### Any stage on its own

- A separate statement of work per stage, sized to one backlog or mandate

- Files in, files out: each stage works alongside your existing systems

- Each stage’s output is the next stage’s input, so adding one later needs no rework

Best for Clients with one pressing problem, or with tools that already cover other stages.

Where are you starting?

## Every conversation starts somewhere

Whatever your entry point, we’ll name the next stage and price it as an option.

> We’re moving to the cloud and don’t know what we have.

- Start with: Discover

- Then expand: Redact, Remediate

> We have to close the file room.

- Start with: Digitize

- Then expand: Remediate, Release

> We can’t keep up with records requests.

- Start with: Redact + Release

- Then expand: Discover, Digitize

> We were told our documents aren’t accessible.

- Start with: Remediate

- Then expand: Digitize, Release

> People need a secure way to ask for their records.

- Start with: Release

- Then expand: Redact, Remediate

> We can’t tell leadership where our backlog stands.

- Start with: Analyze

- Then expand: Discover, Release

Commercial model

## Priced the way the work is measured

Every stage has a clear unit of sale. Bundles are always discounted against the sum of their stages, so the package is always the better buy.

### Discover

Per terabyte scanned

Fixed-fee assessment

### Digitize

Per image, by document type

Backlog project or day-forward service

### Redact

Per page, by review depth

Backlog project or per-request service

### Remediate

Per page, by complexity

Backlog project, then subscription

### Release

Annual fee plus request tiers

Subscription per agency

### Analyze

Per seat, self-hosted licence

Annual subscription

### Ask the Document

Annual fee per site, plus conversation tiers

Add-on subscription to Remediate

Optional add-on

### Full pipeline

Annual fee plus page volume

Multi-year managed service

Best value

Pricing is tailored to each engagement. [Talk to us about a quote](https://www.anacomp.com/contact?topic=pricing)

Title: Introducing the Anacomp Information Lifecycle | Anacomp News
Description: Anacomp unites records discovery, digitization, redaction, accessibility remediation and public release in one pipeline for public agencies.

# Introducing the Anacomp Information Lifecycle

AnnouncementNovember 2026· 4 min read

Public agencies are under four pressures at once: unmapped file estates, paper that can’t be searched, sensitive data in the open, and accessibility obligations. Today we’re bringing our answer together into one pipeline.

The Anacomp Information Lifecycle takes records from raw state to public release. It runs five stages with one analytics layer across all of them, and agencies can buy it end to end or one stage at a time.

## Five stages, one analytics layer

- Discover. Congruity360 scans file systems and cloud repositories for counts, sizes and duplicates.

- Digitize. Anacomp scanning services bring paper into the same flow as digital files.

- Redact. Anacomp redaction, run as workflows on Hyperscience, removes PII and sensitive content.

- Remediate. Anacomp ADA turns any format into data, accessible HTML and tagged documents.

- Release. The Anacomp portal, with ID.me sign-in, lets verified requesters ask and agencies manage and release.

Across every stage, Insignal builds a data warehouse from what the pipeline produces. Staff ask questions in plain English, in the browser or in Teams and Slack, and turn the answers into dashboards and alerts.

## A records request, start to finish

A member of the public verifies their identity with ID.me and asks for documents in the portal. Agency staff pick up the request and find the records, on paper or in file stores. Paper is scanned and indexed, sensitive content is redacted, and ADA produces an accessible copy. The agency approves the release in the portal.

> A record skips any stage it doesn’t need. Born-digital files bypass Digitize, and files with nothing sensitive bypass Redact.

## Two ways to buy

The full pipeline gives one contract and one service level across every stage, with records that never leave Anacomp custody. Any stage on its own is sized to one backlog or mandate and works alongside the systems you already have. Because each stage’s output is the next stage’s input, adding one later needs no rework.

## Start with a 30-day pilot

In week one we scan one repository. In weeks two and three, a sample set of pages runs through Redact and Remediate for your review. In week four, a portal sandbox walks one request from ID.me sign-in to release, all reported in Insignal. The pilot ends with a scoped proposal: the full pipeline, or the stages that proved their value.

[Book a 30-day pilot](https://www.anacomp.com/contact?topic=pilot)

## See it on your own records.

Thirty days, one repository, a sample set of pages and one request walked all the way through.

[Book a pilot](https://www.anacomp.com/contact?topic=pilot)

Title: Zero Trust White Paper on Executive Order 14028 | Anacomp
Description: Anacomp published a white paper by advisory board member Chuck Brooks on meeting DHS and CISA Zero Trust guidance, starting with a data inventory.

# New Zero Trust White Paper on Meeting White House Executive Order 14028 on Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity

White paperMay 2, 2022· 3 min read

Press release from the Anacomp archive, originally published May 2, 2022. Titles and details reflect that date.

A call for an inventory of all data assets as foundational to implementing a Zero Trust Architecture.

Chantilly, VA, United States, May 2, 2022 – Anacomp, a U.S. leading provider of D3 Data Discovery and Visibility solutions to mitigate data breach risk, published a new white paper on How to Meet DHS and CISA Guidelines Supporting White House Executive Order 14028 on Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity. The U.S. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has identified Zero Trust as a shift to a data-centric strategy from a location-centric approach. The white paper addresses this paradigm shift as a call for an inventory of all assets as foundational to implementing a Zero Trust Architecture. Renowned cybersecurity expert and Anacomp Advisory Board member Charles (Chuck) Brooks, President of Brooks Consulting International, is the author of the new white paper.

Risk management of both people and assets regarding data risk is becoming the top cybersecurity imperative, particularly for critical infrastructure and government agencies. On January 26, 2022 the White House announced that the Office of Management and Budget released a federal strategy to move the U.S. government towards a Zero Trust Architecture to support President Biden’s May 12, 2021 Executive Order on Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity. In March 2022, a new Bill, Strengthening American Cybersecurity, was passed with new cyberattack reporting requirements for critical infrastructure.

However, building Zero Trust in organizations represents a significant challenge due to the technology and training required to combat the growing sophistication in cyberthreats. Planning for Zero Trust must start with a strong risk management framework, including a complete inventory of all assets such as data that is at risk. You can’t protect what you don’t know you have. The new white paper addresses the data-centric aspects of Zero Trust.

Chuck Brooks, the white paper’s author, has extensive expertise serving as a two-time presidential appointee, leadership at the Department of Homeland Security, teaching cybersecurity and risk management at Georgetown University, and authoring dozens of articles on cyber tech and policy for publications such as Forbes, Huffington Post, The Hill, and many others. Chuck was named the top person to follow on Tech by LinkedIn and is the President of Brooks Consulting International. He currently serves on Anacomp’s Advisory Board providing strategic guidance on cybersecurity and data protection for our D3 Data Discovery solution.

> “Identification of what is at risk is one of the federal guidelines’ first steps in implementing Zero Trust,” said Tom Cunningham, Anacomp’s CEO. “Our new white paper can help organizations prioritize an actionable inventory of critical assets like data. Anacomp’s D3 Data Discovery solution can aid organizations by automating identification and mitigation of high-value and high-risk unstructured and structured data before damaging data breaches occur.”

To request a copy of the white paper, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

## About Anacomp

Anacomp’s AI/ML D3 Data Discovery Solution enables organizations to shrink their data vulnerability footprint and minimize data breach risk, as well as reduce IT resource and storage costs by identifying and indexing all files – both unstructured and structured – within a single-pane view. Identify every file in your data estate in just days with risk filters and automated metadata that can be instantly searched. View file content and mitigate at-risk data with a risk management workflow. Anacomp has over 50 years of experience serving Fortune 500 companies and federal agencies with innovative digital transformation and data visibility solutions.

For more information, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

Title: Webinar: the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model | Anacomp
Description: Anacomp launched a Zero Trust webinar series, opening with Chuck Brooks, Greg Touhill and Tyler Cohen Wood on the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model.

# New Webinar on the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, The Requirement for a New Data-Centric Cybersecurity Approach

WebinarFebruary 22, 2022· 4 min read

Press release from the Anacomp archive, originally published February 22, 2022. Titles and details reflect that date.

Chantilly, VA, United States, February 22, 2022 – Anacomp, a U.S. leading provider of D3 Data Discovery and Visibility solutions to mitigate data breach risk, announced a new webinar series focused on White House Executive Order 14028 and Federal Zero Trust guidelines on reducing cybersecurity risk. The first webinar will take place on Wednesday, March 23, 2022 at 1 p.m. EDT, and the topic is CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model: The Requirement for a New Data-Centric Cybersecurity Approach. Executives and IT staff from all public and private sectors are invited to register to attend.

Top cybersecurity experts will participate in the webinar including Charles (Chuck) Brooks, President of Brooks Consulting International, Gregory (Greg) Touhill, Director of the CERT Division at the Carnegie Mellon University Software Engineering Institute, and Tyler Cohen Wood, National Security Consultant and VoiceAmerica Talk Show Host.

On January 26, 2022 the White House announced that the Office of Management and Budget released a Federal Strategy to move the U.S. government towards a Zero Trust Architecture to support President Biden’s May 12, 2021 Executive Order on Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity. The FTC has emphasized data security is a board-level responsibility not just an IT problem, and all companies must make it a priority.

The March 23 webinar will focus on the current threat environment, new federal regulations and DHS/CISA guidelines, and tackling the Data Pillar foundation of Zero Trust. Zero Trust is at its core a data-centric strategy emphasizing continuous inventory and protection of all critical assets, including data. You can’t protect what you don’t know you have.

## The panel

Webinar panelists include Chuck Brooks, who has extensive expertise serving as a two-time presidential appointee, leadership at the Department of Homeland Security, teaching cybersecurity and risk management at Georgetown University, and authoring dozens of articles on cyber tech and policy for publications such as Forbes, Huffington Post, The Hill, and many others. Chuck was named the top person to follow on Tech by LinkedIn and is the President of Brooks Consulting International. He currently serves on Anacomp’s Advisory Board providing strategic guidance on cybersecurity and data protection for our D3 Data Discovery solution.

Greg Touhill has decades of experience in high-profile cybersecurity positions. He was appointed by former President Barack Obama to be the first Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) of the U.S. government. Previously, he served in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) as Deputy Assistant Secretary in the Office of Cybersecurity and Communications. Touhill is a 30-year veteran of the U.S. Air Force and he served as a senior leader of military cybersecurity and information technology programs, including the position of Chief Information Officer of the U.S. Transportation Command. In addition to directing the world-renowned CERT division at the Software Engineering Institute, Greg is also an adjunct faculty member of the CMU Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy and the Deakin University (Australia) Centre for Cybersecurity Research and Innovation.

Tyler Cohen Wood is also participating on the panel, and she has over 20 years of highly technical experience, including 13 years working for the Department of Defense (DoD). Tyler helped the White House, DoD, federal law enforcement, and the intelligence community thwart many threats to U.S. cybersecurity. She sits on several global advisory boards such as the Global Cybersecurity Association, EC-Council Incident Handlers global board amongst others. Tyler is also a top cybersecurity influencer and is currently the host of a brand-new live talk show called My Connected Life on the VoiceAmerica network to discuss all the latest cyber hot button issues.

> “Anacomp is excited to bring these three cybersecurity leaders together for our first webinar on helping organizations navigate the new Federal guidance on implementing Zero Trust Architecture,” said Tom Cunningham, Anacomp’s CEO. “Zero Trust focuses on data protection, and it assumes that breaches will occur due to the prevalence of phishing and social engineering. To minimize risk, all critical data assets must be proactively inventoried and mitigated before breach. Anacomp’s D3 Data Discovery solution can help organizations quickly identify and protect high-value and high-risk unstructured and structured data before damaging data breaches.”

## About Anacomp

Anacomp’s D3 Data Discovery Solution enables organizations to reduce growing data breach costs as well as IT resource and data storage costs by identifying and organizing all files – both unstructured and structured – within a single pane view so that files can be efficiently moved, encrypted or deleted. Start identifying every file in your data estate in as quickly as a day with risk filters and automated, detailed metadata that can be instantly searched. View file content and place at-risk data into a risk management workflow. Anacomp has over 50 years of experience serving Fortune 500 companies and federal agencies with innovative digital transformation and data visibility solutions.

For more information, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

# Chuck Brooks, Cybersecurity & Emerging Technology Leader, Joins Anacomp’s Advisory Board

AnnouncementNovember 17, 2021· 3 min read

Press release from the Anacomp archive, originally published November 17, 2021. Titles and details reflect that date.

Chantilly, VA, United States, November 17, 2021 – Anacomp, a U.S. leading provider of D3 Data Discovery and data visibility solutions to reduce cybersecurity, privacy and compliance risks, announced that Charles (Chuck) Brooks has joined Anacomp’s Strategic Advisory Board. Chuck is a globally recognized cybersecurity and emerging technology thought leader and has been a leading evangelist for cybersecurity in both the public and private sectors for decades. He was named the top person to follow on Tech by LinkedIn.

Chuck’s extensive expertise includes serving as a two-time presidential appointee, leadership at the Department of Homeland Security as the first Director of Legislative Affairs, teaching cybersecurity and risk management at John Hopkins University and Georgetown University, and authoring dozens of articles on cyber tech and policy for publications such as Forbes, Huffington Post, The Hill, Federal Times, and many others. Chuck is also President of Brooks Consulting International and has served as an adviser and renowned public speaker to Capitol Hill, for corporations such as General Dynamics and Xerox, and for nonprofit organizations including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

As a strategic advisor, Chuck will provide guidance to Anacomp’s leadership team on cybersecurity and compliance focusing on D3’s cybersecurity, Zero Trust, and data protection capabilities for the national infrastructure and energy sectors. Chuck’s thought leadership and writings on cybersecurity and emerging technology have helped shape the public policy debate and he has been a force in advocating for cybersecurity issues across digital media, at events, in professional forums, and with a variety of public policy organizations.

> “Anacomp is delighted to have Chuck join our leadership team,” said Tom Cunningham, Anacomp’s CEO. “Chuck is a highly respected global cybersecurity leader, and his depth of expertise and perspective will help guide the D3 Data Discovery Solution as a foundational data-centric cybersecurity tool for combating rising ransomware and data breach risk and costs.”

With average ransomware attacks costing an astounding $4.62M, Anacomp’s goal is to help organizations quickly identify and take action to protect high value and high risk unstructured and structured data before breach occurs.

## About Anacomp

Anacomp’s D3 Data Discovery Solution enables organizations to reduce growing data breach costs as well as IT resource and data storage costs by identifying and organizing all files – both unstructured and structured – within a single pane view so that files can be efficiently moved, encrypted or deleted. Start identifying every file in your data estate in as quickly as a day with risk filters and automated, detailed metadata that can be instantly searched. View file content and place at-risk data into a risk management workflow. Anacomp has over 50 years of experience serving Fortune 500 companies and federal agencies with innovative digital transformation and data visibility solutions.

For more information, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

URL: https://www.anacomp.com/news/grs-anacomp-950m-air-force-abms-contract
Title: GRS and Anacomp Win $950M Air Force ABMS Contract | Anacomp
Description: Government Research Specialists and technology partner Anacomp won a $950M-ceiling U.S. Air Force IDIQ contract for ABMS and JADC2 data discovery.

# GRS and Technology Partner Anacomp Awarded $950M Ceiling IDIQ Contract by the U.S. Air Force to Support Data Discovery for Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS)

Contract awardAugust 25, 2021· 3 min read

Press release from the Anacomp archive, originally published August 25, 2021. Titles and details reflect that date.

Bethesda, MD, United States, August 25, 2021 – Government Research Specialists (GRS), a U.S. leading research and solutions consultant to Federal agencies, with strategic partner, Anacomp, Inc., was awarded a $950M ceiling indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract by the U.S. Air Force to develop data discovery capabilities across all operations.

GRS’s technology solutions will support the maturation, demonstration and proliferation of capability across platforms and domains, leveraging open systems design, modern software and algorithm development in order to enable Joint All Domain Command and Control (JADC2). The contract is part of a multiple award multi-level security effort to provide development and operation of systems as a unified force across all domains (air, land, sea, space, cyber, and electromagnetic spectrum) in an open architecture family of systems that enables capabilities via multiple integrated platforms.

GRS is working with technology partner, Anacomp, Inc., to deliver the D3 Data Discovery & Distillation Solution to further the systems unification goals of JADC2 to enable data-driven decision-making using all types of data, from any source and at any location.

> “The D3 Solution provides the flexibility to see, control and unlock the power of data across all data stores, from remote container environments to operations centers. We are proud to be selected to support the technology needs of the USAF and JADC2,” said Mike Hogan, Chief Operating Officer, GRS.

D3 takes advantage of cutting-edge artificial intelligence and machine-learning capabilities to run autonomously with unsupervised tools that can process datasets and assign metadata without a large burden of resources.

> “Anacomp’s D3 Data Discovery engine is a fully scalable and modular solution, offering real-time, accurate and fast integration of petabyte volumes of both unstructured and structured data. D3 delivers data customized to the mission,” said Tom Cunningham, Anacomp’s Chief Executive Officer.

This contract continues both GRS’s and Anacomp’s long-term, supportive role with the DoD and other Federal agency customers who require solutions that provide high-level security, accuracy and deliver ROI. U.S. forces depend on data at their fingertips, and platforms like D3 bring those capabilities into reality.

## About GRS and Anacomp, Inc.

GRS is the research and consulting division of Government Sales Specialists, the largest Federal consultant working with agency officials for over 15 years to help simplify and accelerate the procurement of innovative IT solutions.

Anacomp has over 50 years of experience serving Federal agencies with cutting-edge digital transformation and data visibility solutions.

For more information, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

# Anacomp and Exonar Announce Strategic Partnership to Deliver Intelligent Data Discovery Services in U.S.

PartnershipFebruary 24, 2021· 2 min read

Press release from the Anacomp archive, originally published February 24, 2021. Titles and details reflect that date.

Chantilly, VA, United States, February 24, 2021 – Anacomp, Inc. (OTCBB: ANMP), a leading provider of technology-based records and data governance and document management solutions, and Exonar Limited announced a formal partnership agreement to deliver intelligent data discovery services to the U.S. federal government agencies and commercial organizations.

All organizations face both the challenge and opportunity of owning large quantities of data and implementing a strong data management and governance strategy. By combining Anacomp’s specialized expertise and experience implementing document management solutions with Exonar’s world-leading data discovery software, we can capture, classify and index large data estates efficiently.

> “The addition of Exonar to our Data Discovery and Distillation (D3) service offering is a keystone to delivering intelligent automation support for records governance, cloud migration and digital transformation initiatives for our government and commercial customers. With Exonar’s Reveal platform we offer our customers the powerful ability to build a complete index of billions of data items, particularly unstructured data, to achieve regulatory compliance and privacy protection.” — Thomas Cunningham, Anacomp CEO

> “By combining our data discovery capabilities with Anacomp’s proven success in the Federal Government and commercial space, we look forward to helping organizations improve business processes, reduce costs and achieve compliance.” — Danny Reeves, CEO, Exonar

Both parties are excited about this new partnership and the many potential benefits it holds for federal agencies and commercial customers.

## About Anacomp, Inc.

Anacomp is a leading provider of technology-based solutions for data discovery and governance, digital transformation, and records and information management. We have helped federal agencies and commercial customers improve business processes, reduce costs and achieve compliance for over 50 years. Anacomp is based in Chantilly, VA with regional offices across the U.S.

## About Exonar

As data discovery experts we believe that your data should power and protect organizations and the people you serve. Exonar’s powerful software helps our customers find and understand the billions of items of data and information they hold and how to extract real value from it.

For more information, [contact Anacomp](https://www.anacomp.com/contact).

# Let’s talk about your records.

Book a pilot, get pricing for a stage, or just tell us where it hurts. A real person replies within one business day.

### What happens next

- We reply within one business day to set up a short call.

- We learn about your records, backlog and mandates.

- You get a pilot plan or a priced proposal for the stages you need.

### Public-sector buyers

Ask us about contract vehicles, security authorizations and procurement paperwork. We’ll send what your process needs.

Questions

## Before you get in touch

Do we have to buy the whole pipeline?
No. Every stage is complete on its own and works alongside your existing systems: files in, files out. Because each stage’s output is the next stage’s input, adding another later needs no rework.

What does the 30-day pilot include?
Week 1: Discover scans one repository you choose. Weeks 2–3: a sample set of pages runs through Redact and Remediate for your review. Week 4: a portal sandbox walks one request from ID.me sign-in to release, with the pilot reported in Insignal. It ends with a scoped proposal.

How is each stage priced?
Each stage has its own unit of sale: per terabyte for Discover, per image for Digitize, per page for Redact and Remediate, an annual fee plus request tiers for Release, per seat for Analyze, and an annual fee plus conversation tiers for the Ask the Document add-on. Bundles are discounted against the sum of their stages.

Do our records leave our control?
On the full pipeline, records move from stage to stage without leaving Anacomp custody, so there are no hand-offs between vendors to secure. Insignal is self-hosted in your own cloud.

Which technology is inside?
Congruity360 for Discover, Hyperscience workflows for Redact, ID.me for identity in the Release portal, and Insignal for Analyze. Anacomp integrates and operates them all.
